title: Chicago as the Wild West versus New York sophistication
summary: Chicago players played wide open from the heart but lacked New York's artistic sophistication.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You were in an interesting position because you came to New York first and worked there for a while, staid in the Cecil Hotel and then, right after that, you went with Tiny Bradshaw back to Chicago, in the Rum Boogie, and I just wonder if anything by way of contrast with the two scenes, at that time Chicago and New York,/struck your attention.
Well, Chicago's like the Wild West. You know, people played from their heart but it wasn't that sophis-

tication that you get, musically, in New York. I mean everybody played good, everybody, but it was like it was the West, you know what I mean, and everybody played wide open. They played good but it didn't have that artistic sophistication that New York has, you know what I mean. Everybody was happy, but they didn't have that New York sophistication.
